newsitem.title: USA: Hartford Whalers to decide soon on arena - report.
newsitem.headline: Hartford Whalers to decide soon on arena - report.

text.p: The owner of the National Hockey League's Hartford Whalers will decide within the next week whether to accept the state's latest proposal to help build a new arena or move out of Connecticut, the Hartford Courant reported on Friday.
Republican Governor John Rowland has made his final and best offer to owner Peter Karmanos to keep the Whalers in the capital city, the report said.
"It's really up to them to make a business decision about whether to stay or not," Rowland said. He said there was a 50-50 chance the Whalers would stay.

One of the biggest stumbling blocks in the talks is finding a way to cover the Whalers' financial losses during the years when the arena is being built. Since the arena could take up to three years to construct, the losses of $15 million per year could total $45 million before the new venue opens.
Another factor is the need to lease about 80 luxury skyboxes at a time when the Hartford Civic Center has leased only about 30 of the available 45 skyboces.
The Whalers have said they will leave Connecticut unless the state helps fund a new arena that could cost more than $160 million.
Other cities said to be interested in luring the team are St. Paul, Minn., and Columbus, Ohio.
